thread:
anya: FYI ran a headroom sweep this morning comparing small microbatch sizes vs slightly higher max_wait headroom. paste of key numbers below.

sam: nice, what kernel variants were in the mix?

anya: single-GEMM quantized + fallback to fp16 attention kernel. tested kernel A (fast softmax) and kernel B (stable numerics) — results diverged on tails.

devon: can you drop the top-line p95/p99s?

anya: Sure. baseline (max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=5): p95=28ms, p99=110ms, throughput=650 tok/s.

anya: microbatch-small (max_batch_tokens=1024, max_wait_ms=2): p95=18ms, p99=210ms, throughput=420 tok/s.

anya: microbatch-large+wait (max_batch_tokens=8192, max_wait_ms=10): p95=35ms, p99=95ms, throughput=880 tok/s.

olga: interesting — microbatch-small has lower p95 but p99 exploded. suggests long-tail queueing when rare long requests block the batch?

sam: does KV cache behavior change across these? cache hit ratio or prefix reuse could affect this.

anya: yes — KV hit rate for microbatch-small dropped to 54% on that workload vs 78% baseline. small batches increase cache churn.

devon: do you have profiling traces for the p99 cases? stack traces or stage timings?

anya: pasted sample trace from perf-bot:
```
TRACE 1968001234 tx=0x7f: queue_wait=140ms, batch_build=4ms, kernel_run=8ms, kv_update=12ms, fallback_kernel=0ms
TRACE 1968001240 tx=0x9a: queue_wait=10ms, batch_build=3ms, kernel_run=80ms, kv_update=10ms
```

anya: first line typical tail: long queue_wait -> small kernel_run; second line is heavy kernel-run path (long sequence) but short queue wait.

olga: that supports headroom idea: small microbatches reduce average queue time but increase probability that a slow-inference request sits alone and stretches tail when it does happen.

sam: any differences in kernel fallback frequency? kernel B fallback rate?

anya: fallback to kernel B increased slightly with microbatch-small: 3.7% vs 2.1% baseline. Kernel selection more brittle with fewer tokens per batch.

perf-bot: perf summary uploaded to /tmp/headroom-sweep-1968001234.csv (p95,p99,throughput,kvcache,fallback_rate per config).

devon: do we have SLO targets? remember prod p99 target = 120ms.

anya: yes prod p99 SLO=120ms. microbatch-small violated SLO on tails. microbatch-large+wait kept p99 < 100ms but increased p95 beyond some client targets.

olga: tradeoff mapping: if we raise max_wait_ms from 5->10 with moderate batch tokens, we get better p99 (fewer tiny batches) at cost of p95 bump. Can we do adaptive wait: dynamic max_wait that drops when queue length short?

sam: idea: use tail-aware wait_ms where we track recent queue_wait samples and increase wait_ms if p99 rising. cheap moving window.

devon: also consider small 'headroom slots' reserved for long sequences so they don't pollute normal batches. e.g., if seq_len>thresh, route to slow lane with dedicated capacity.

anya: prototyped a scheduler param: "burst_headroom_tokens=2048" that keeps a small reserved token budget to absorb long queries; helped p99 fall ~18% in experiment.

olga: nice. any regression in throughput or KV metrics?

anya: tiny throughput dip (~3%) and KV hit rate unchanged vs baseline. tail improved more consistently.

sam: how about combining adaptive wait + headroom? sounds promising.

anya: ran a 2h combo: p95=30ms, p99=88ms, throughput=840 tok/s, KV hit=76%, fallback_rate=1.9%.

devon: those numbers look production-viable. need canary with realistic multi-tenant mix.

olga: also add kernel-selection logging to better attribute long kernel_run vs queue_wait; current attribution ambiguous in ~12% of tails.

anya: noted. I'm adding a lightweight tag in runtime traces to say "reserved-slot" vs "normal" + kernel id.

sam: can you open a short PR with config knobs and perf test? include docs for headroom rationale and expected tradeoffs.

anya: will do. PR after code review, then canary on staging.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/scheduler:v2.8-headroom-sweep -> staging at 1968001800 by anya :white_check_mark:

devon: thanks everyone. one follow-up: set alert if p99 > 120ms for 5m in canary.

anya: added alert rule. will post results after 2h canary.

sam: awesome work, great investigative pattern. :+1:
